decisive_items: a 10.6×5.0×5.6-cm heterogeneous pericardial mass invading the right atrium
a large echodense mass in the right atrium
hepatic vein thrombosis and reversal of portal venous flow
response.rationale: The pericardial mass invading the right atrium is the primary lesion, explaining the right atrial mass and extensive venous thrombosis (including hepatic vein and IVC) as tumor thrombus. Budd-Chiari syndrome is a secondary manifestation of the tumor thrombus, not the underlying diagnosis.

rejected.why: Hepatic vein thrombosis is present but is a consequence of the tumor thrombus extending from the pericardial mass; lacks the primary neoplastic cause.
Hepatorenal syndrome is a complication of the liver failure, not the underlying diagnosis.
IVC thrombosis is part of the thrombotic burden but does not account for the pericardial mass and right atrial invasion.
